name: WOTS Up 2
scheme: Plain Winternitz (w=256, SHA-256, KEY_LEN=32) in chal.py — no tweak/r values in the actual attachment; chain: pub[i]=H^256(priv[i]), sig[i]=H^(255-h_i)(priv[i]), verify: H^(h_i+1)(sig[i])==pub[i]
attack: One-way hash chains allow lowering digest bytes only: from any valid sig[i]=H^(255-m_j_i)(priv_i) one can derive H^(255-t_i)(priv_i) for any t_i<=m_j_i by extra hashing. With 20 given signatures, per-coordinate max over signatures covers target digest bytes. Target message2 = '<pubkey0.hex()> sent 999999 WOTScoins to me' is deterministic from public_key[0]; its SHA-256 digest t_i satisfied t_i <= max_j m_j_i for all 32 coordinates, so the forged signature (first usable signature j with m_j_i>=t_i, extended by digs[j][i]-t_i hashes) is bit-identical to the real signature2.
flag_recovery: aes_key = first byte of each forged chain element (matches chal.py), AES-256-CBC decrypt of data.json 'enc' with 'iv' -> 32-byte plaintext flag.
verification: All 20 provided signatures re-verified against public_key; forged signature passed verify(forged, message2) == public_key; decrypted plaintext is clean ASCII FLAG-REDACTED-SEE-FLAGS-MIRROR (no padding artifacts).
